subject: Packaging guardrails & tariff unwind — CloudHealth plan options
messages:
From: Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging review — immediate downgrade question

Hey Grace,

Quick note from our side — our usage has dropped ~35% this month due to a pause in a pilot. We need to explore a short-term downgrade or a credit arrangement while we stabilize. Key asks:

- Can we temporarily move from Tier A (reserved throughput) to Tier B (metered) without losing feature entitlements?
- What happens to seat-level addons (audit logs, long-retention) if we switch tiers mid-term?
- Any precedent for a short-term discount or transitional credit?

We want to avoid a contract amendment if possible — looking for billing-friendly packaging options or a pilot-style stepdown. Would appreciate concrete options + ballpark numbers so procurement can review.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Ramirez | Head of Cloud Integrations
CloudHealth

[Attachment: CloudHealth_Usage_Q3_sample.csv (csv)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging review — immediate downgrade question

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up and the sample usage. Sorry to hear the pilot paused. Short answer: yes, we can offer a guarded downgrade path that preserves your addons and audit data for a limited window, plus a transitional credit option. Longer answer below.

Options (high level):

1) Soft-step to Metered (30-day protected window)
   - Move Tier A -> Tier B immediately; retained addon entitlements (audit logs, long-retention) remain active for 30 days.
   - Billing: new metered overage pricing applies; we apply a one-time transition credit equal to 20% of expected monthly reserved commitment for first month.

2) Temporary Seat Reduction with Feature Holdback
   - Keep Tier A but reduce reserved seats for 60 days. Addons remain, but throughput SLA no longer applies to reduced seats.
   - Billing: prorated reserved charge + option for one-time 10% concession on the prorated amount.

3) Pilot-Fallback (90 days)
   - Convert to a Pilot license: metered pricing, full retention of features, and an extended support cadence. Pricing: blended rate between Tier A and Tier B; requires short amendment.

Questions for you so we can scope numbers:
- Which addons must remain unchanged (audit logs, retention, encryption KMS?).
- Expected runway for the pilot pause (4–8 weeks, multi-month?).

I can get Ben to run specific P&L scenarios and Marissa to draft the short amendment language if you want.

If helpful, can we do a 30-minute call today to agree the path? I have 3:00pm PT free.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: redwood-pricing-options-CH-4392.xlsx]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging review — immediate downgrade question

Sophie — looping in some quick numbers so you have a ballpark ahead of procurement review. Grace gave the right constructs; here are scenario estimates using your Q3 sample: 

- Soft-step to Metered (30-day protected window): estimated bill next month = $38k (vs reserved $52k). One-time transition credit = $10k applied to next invoice.
- Temporary Seat Reduction (30% seats): prorated reserved charge = $37k; 10% concession ≈ $3.7k.
- Pilot-Fallback (90 days): blended rate ≈ $0.65/token across forecasted tokens = $29k; requires 1-page amendment.

Notes / constraints:
- We hold audit logs and retention flags for 90 days after downgrade; beyond that, retention will be subject to the lower-tier defaults unless you explicitly extend.
- KMS/HSM key access is tied to contract entitlements; we can preserve access during the Pilot-Fallback but must list that in the short amendment.

If Sophie confirms which addons are non-negotiable and how long the pause will be, I can prepare a formal quote for procurement.

Ben Carter
Lead, Account Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Ramirez <sophie.ramirez@cloudhealth.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging review — immediate downgrade question

Thanks Grace/Ben — this is helpful. Quick answers:

- Must preserve: audit logs (7 year retention), KMS access for keys, and long-term embeddings retention.
- Runway: likely 6 weeks, could be 8.
- Preference: Soft-step to Metered with the 30-day protected window to buy time and avoid an amendment.

Procurement will want the exact credit math and a short note that entitlements are preserved for at least 60 days for those specified items (we need 60 to be safe). Also, any language that guarantees we can move back to Tier A with prior pricing within 120 days would be ideal.

Can you provide a 1-page summary with the numbers and sample contract wording? We can loop procurement after that.

Sophie
